title: Derived internal Hom and localization of a bounded localization complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, and use module sheaves and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a section $g$, write $\mathcal O[1/g]$ for the sheafification of $V\mapsto\mathcal O(V)[1/g|_V]$, and write $\mathcal O_U$ for the restriction to the slice site $\mathcal C/U$. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex whose terms are finite direct sums of such localizations (including $\mathcal O=\mathcal O[1/1]$), and let $N\in D(\mathcal O)$. Derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] commutes with slice restriction:
$$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(P,N)|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(P|_U,N|_U).$$
For any object $U$ and $f\in\mathcal O(U)$ let $P_f^\bullet=\mathcal O_U[1/f]\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}P^\bullet|_U$, with the differential obtained by tensoring. This ordinary complex represents $\mathcal O_U[1/f]\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_U}P|_U$; a summand $\mathcal O_U[1/g]$ becomes $\mathcal O_U[1/(fg)]$. Here the derived tensor is the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after a K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(P|_U,N|_U))\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(P_f,N|_U),$$
natural in $N$ and chain maps of $P$, and compatible with further slice restriction. These assertions impose no boundedness condition on $N$.

proof.text: Reuse the unchanged explicit localization and derived models. Sectionwise localization flatness, sheafification, finite coproducts and exact slice restriction prove the K-flat certificates. The single-total-tensor comparison and the already proved product-localization calculation give the ordinary-complex derived-tensor model and summand calculation. These declarations are reexported from RingedLocalizationModels without a change in their meaning.

Use the canonical K-flat currying natural isomorphism, transported through exact restriction and the single-total-tensor comparison. Naturality of that natural isomorphism supplies exactly the chain-map and derived-target naturality equation of the statement.

Restrict the localization coefficient by its canonical fraction-presheaf and sheafification comparison. The coefficient and ordinary tensor-complex derived transports are the explicit comparisons constructed from this sheaf isomorphism. Specialize preservation of the fixed model currying comparison to those localization coefficients and to the proved K-flat certificates. The component formula for the natural currying comparison identifies it with modelCurryIso, giving the displayed further-restriction equation and the successive restriction law.
